clue.text: Dog's polite greeting a sensation

definitions.note: read as 'Dog is': a child's word for a dog

parts.note: a bow is a courteous greeting
a wow is a sensational success

explanation.surface: A dog makes a courteous gesture of greeting that causes a stir.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Dog's' is 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Nursery speech names a dog after its bark, so a child calls the animal by that name.

clue.text: Having crossed lobby, called out for service

parts.note: over means having crossed, as in being over the road

indicators.note: tells us the word is spoken, so we hear it

parts.note: a hall is an entrance lobby

explanation.surface: Someone crosses the lobby and is summoned to a service.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorough check and repair of a car or machine is a full service.

clue.text: Lead blew out, but thus possible to repair?

indicators.note: out means wrong or broken, so the letters of lead blew are reordered

explanation.surface: A lead fuse has blown, but perhaps it can be fixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal that can be fused by heat can be repaired that way, so it is mendable.

clue.text: The road to it wearing out with constant interruption

definitions.note: Orwell's book The Road to Wigan Pier names the destination

indicators.note: the constant interrupts, breaking into the middle of the jumbled letters
out signals the letters of wearing are rearranged

parts.note: pi is the mathematical constant

explanation.surface: A road worn out by constant breaks for roadworks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interruption' puts PI into WIGANER, the anagram of WEARING from 'out'. Wigan is a town in northern England, made famous by Orwell's book.
explanation.definitionFit: George Orwell's book title supplies this place as the destination of the road.

clue.text: But the others have springs too

definitions.text: But the others have springs too

parts.words: But the others have springs too
parts.note: a jumping year might be thought the only one with springs, but every year has a spring season

explanation.surface: Something with bounce is being compared with others that are just as springy.
explanation.definitionFit: The extra-day year sounds like it involves jumping, yet every calendar year includes the season of spring.

clue.text: They think men closely and boringly confined here?

definitions.text: They think men closely and boringly confined here?

parts.words: They think men closely and boringly confined here?
parts.note: brain cells do the thinking; a dull grey small prison cell would confine men closely and boringly

explanation.surface: Prisoners kept in cramped, dreary cells.
explanation.walkthrough: Hercule Poirot's phrase for his brain doubles as small, dull prison cells.
explanation.definitionFit: Agatha Christie's detective Poirot credits his brain's grey matter with the thinking.

clue.text: TV critic often given this page, adding this

indicators.note: adding puts the critic's write-up after the letter for page

parts.note: here 'this' is what a TV critic produces, a review

explanation.surface: A television reviewer typically receives something, with a page attached.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'this' words point at what a critic deals in: the first at the advance showing, the second at the critic's write-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Critics are often shown programmes in advance so they can write about them before broadcast.

clue.text: Fabulous place in east with funny old road

indicators.note: funny means odd, so the letters of old road are rearranged

explanation.surface: A legendary spot in the East reached by a quaint old road.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary city of gold sought by explorers is a mythical, fabulous place.

clue.text: Boy survived sprain

parts.note: rode, as in rode out a storm, means survived
a rick is a sprain or wrench

explanation.surface: A lad came through an injury.
explanation.definitionFit: A male first name, so an example of a boy's name.

clue.text: No-go district?

parts.note: a traffic signal meaning stop is a 'no-go' light, and the phrase also names a district for prostitution

explanation.surface: An area where people dare not enter.
explanation.definitionFit: The stop signal at traffic lights forbids going, and the same colour labels a district of brothels.

clue.text: People were killed, not one cured

parts.note: men means people

indicators.note: 'not' tells us to drop the letter for 'one' from the dying word

parts.note: died means were killed
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A grim report: people were killed and nobody was healed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cured, like a mended rift or injury, has been made whole again; a synonym.

clue.text: Her plans shot in pieces

indicators.note: plans that are shot are ruined, so the letters of her plans are scrambled

explanation.surface: A woman's plans have been shattered into fragments.
explanation.definitionFit: Shell fragments thrown out by an explosion are pieces of metal.

clue.text: Paper for hanging on the wall?

definitions.meaning: the Daily ... is a British tabloid newspaper
a looking glass is something you hang on a wall

explanation.surface: Wallpaper, it seems, being chosen for decorating.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests wallpaper; in fact the paper is the Daily Mirror, a British tabloid.
explanation.definitionFit: A British tabloid carries this name, and a looking glass is commonly hung on a wall.

clue.text: Dishonest and mean, get hiding

parts.note: lying means dishonest
low means mean or base

explanation.surface: A shifty, nasty character goes into concealment.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep out of sight and avoid notice is an idiom for being in hiding.

clue.text: Concerned with coping, being liable to arrest

parts.note: of means concerning, as in 'tales of'
fending, as in fending for oneself, means coping

explanation.surface: Someone worried about managing who might be arrested.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaking the law, committing a crime, is what makes a person liable to arrest.

clue.text: Escape shaft got off the ground, so to speak

indicators.note: tells us the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: flew means got off the ground

explanation.surface: Something escaping up a shaft and taking off into the air.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimney duct lets smoke and gases escape upward, a shaft for exhaust.

clue.text: Sudden gathering, not necessarily smartly turned out?

definitions.meaning: a crowd organised to appear suddenly in public
read as a flashy crowd, flash being slang for showily smart, yet its members need not dress up

explanation.surface: An impromptu crowd that has not dressed up.
explanation.definitionFit: A crowd summoned by phone or social media to gather briefly and suddenly in public.

clue.text: Blow to have part of shoe removed

parts.note: the upper is the top part of a shoe
cut means removed, as a scene is cut

explanation.surface: A cobbler's misfortune: part of the shoe has been taken off.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxing punch thrown upward to the chin is a kind of blow.

clue.text: Thump husband out of alarm

indicators.note: the letter for husband is taken out of the word for alarm

parts.note: shock means alarm

explanation.surface: A husband is punched, startled out of fright.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a hard blow or punch, so a synonym for a thump.

clue.text: Friend's turned up then all but hurried away, giving barely a word

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: an ally is a friend, plus the 's

indicators.note: all but means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: blew, slang for left in a hurry

explanation.surface: A friend appears, then rushes off having barely said anything.
explanation.definitionFit: A single unit of sound is hardly even a word, often less than one.

clue.text: Bone from one hanging in the cold, executed, thrown across small room

indicators.note: the shortened word is thrown across, around, the word for a small room
executed means beheaded, so the first letter goes

parts.note: an icicle hangs from eaves in freezing weather
lav, short for lavatory, is a small room

explanation.surface: A grisly scene of a body hung in the cold, executed and flung across a tiny room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Executed' means beheaded, leaving CICLE, which is then thrown across the small room's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The collarbone is a bone linking shoulder blade and breastbone.

clue.text: Little pest flourished, invested in renewable energy

indicators.note: the abbreviation is put inside, invested in, the reworked letters
renewable means the letters of energy can be made anew in another order

parts.note: fl. abbreviates floruit, Latin for 'flourished', used of when a person was active

explanation.surface: A small pest thrived by putting money into green power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Renewable energy' looks like one green phrase, but 'renewable' is the anagram signal, making GREENY; fl. (floruit) is the dictionary abbreviation for 'flourished'.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphids are tiny garden insects that damage plants, a small pest by example.

clue.text: Listen — I have got inside clothes

indicators.note: the contraction for I have is put inside the word for clothes

parts.note: gear means clothes
I've is I have

explanation.surface: A listener announcing they have got into some outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay attention and hear someone out is an idiom for listening.

clue.text: Don't say it: fairies are short, and slowly get lower

parts.note: sh is the call for silence

indicators.note: short means the last letter is cut off the word for fairies

parts.note: elves are fairies

explanation.surface: Someone is hushed on the touchy subject of the fairies' height.
explanation.definitionFit: Land that slopes away gradually is said to do this, descending by degrees.

clue.text: Politician in chamber left for selection meeting

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative

indicators.note: the letter for left goes in the word for a chamber

parts.note: a cave is an underground chamber

explanation.surface: A politician in the House chamber leaves for a candidate selection meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinals gather in secret session to choose a pope, the classic gathering to select.

clue.text: Mouse one may take as a joke

definitions.text: one may take as a joke
definitions.meaning: to take the ... is to tease or mock, British slang

explanation.surface: A rodent that someone might laugh off.
explanation.definitionFit: Disney's cartoon rodent carries this name, and British slang 'take the ___' means tease someone.

clue.text: Relaxed face?

parts.note: a clock's face is its dial, and those letters ..., written backwards, spell laid

explanation.surface: A calm expression.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: LAID set backwards gives DIAL, a face.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone easygoing and unhurried is relaxed; an informal synonym.

clue.text: Cask on ship for support

parts.note: a butt is a large cask
re means on or concerning
SS is steamship

explanation.surface: A barrel stands aboard a vessel as a prop.
explanation.definitionFit: A projecting structure of masonry supports a wall, and figuratively any support.

clue.text: Good domestic appliance left by father for chap

indicators.note: the letters for father leave the appliance's name

parts.note: a freezer is a kitchen appliance
Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest

explanation.surface: A kitchen appliance abandoned by Dad for some fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a man or fellow, the same as chap.
